rationale: Round 8 resolves every round-7 R4 elision-evidence ask by taking the expressly admissible alternative (b) in place: the false exactly-once claim is withdrawn where it appeared, the protocol is now explicitly at-least-once, and each replayable operation has a sufficient one-line idempotence/convergence argument. R overwrites the index from the current tip without touching the worktree or refs; S exports ADR-0025's deterministic current Dolt projection; dirt classification is read-only and refuses on current genuine dirt; merge reuses spec 127's preserved-merge/ancestry convergence. The absent-to-D CREATE route and both-elided no-marker route close the transition graph. Fixtures xviii, xix, and xx inject the three previously absent interruption shapes and require observable rerun/convergence behavior, making replay falsifiable at bead implementation review. The unchanged R4 checks also pass: plan validation exits 0 with only the three acknowledged decomposition warnings, work_chunks parses and maps positionally/dependency-wise to Beads 1-10, and OQ-3 still mechanically yields stored==derived across plan approval, lifecycle claim, and the non-lifecycle trigger-2 window. No remaining defect would corrupt a bead's implementation.

findings.summary: The prior partial discriminator finding is resolved by withdrawing exactly-once rather than pretending elided stages leave durable evidence. Existing C/D commits remain trailer-classified, while missing commits are governed by the explicit at-least-once replay contract.

The no-op-D crash window is now described truthfully: tip==marker==C re-enters through R and S, and both are allowed to replay. R's mixed reset converges to the same index; S's unchanged-state export converges to identical artifact bytes; the S-exit route remains mandatory before merge.

The empty-C and both-elided boundaries are complete. When C elides, first publication may CREATE a D marker parenting A with the same CAS refusal. When both stages elide, no marker or ref movement is claimed; interruption re-enters as an ordinary run and replay is permitted.

Fixtures xviii-xx cover the exact missing interruption points: after R with C elided and before D publication; after no-op S/D elision and before merge with marker C present; and both stages elided before merge. They require ordinary rerun or explicit R/S replay plus convergence, while xvii retains ordinary-D trailer coverage.

All four short proofs are implementation-usable. ResetIndexToHead is an overwrite-to-current-tip operation; export is a deterministic projection and is forward-correct if authoritative Dolt state advances; classification is a pure observation/refusal; and merge delegates to the already-pinned spec-127 convergence machinery. None relies on recovering evidence that elision did not persist.
